title: Researchers Prepare Bell States with Extremely Low Error Rates Approaching One in Ten Thousand
key_facts: Researchers at Universitat de Barcelona (Jordi Comelles and colleagues) propose an analogue method to prepare Bell states in superconducting circuits
Reports infidelities as low as about 10 to the minus 4 (one in ten thousand)
Preparation takes roughly 100 nanoseconds, comparable to digital methods (80 to 130 ns)
Typical digital methods give errors around 10 to the minus 3
Uses adiabatic interpolation and resonant population transfer instead of discrete gates
Performance depends on realistic parameters that are not fully defined
Authors say further work must define limits for scaling beyond small systems; paper on arXiv 2609.09013 (author named Ana Palacios)
quote_evidence: It now reaches infidelities on the order of 10-4 within approximately 100 nanoseconds.
While performance relies on realistic parameters, these are not fully defined and establishing those limits is vital for assessing scalability.
why_it_matters_hint: A possible gentler route to very accurate entangled pairs, but shown only for small systems and under assumed parameters.
event_date: not stated (arXiv number suggests a September 2026 submission)
notes: The article does not clearly say whether the result is a hardware experiment or a theoretical analysis; the caveat on 'realistic parameters' suggests modelling. Author naming differs in the article (Comelles vs Palacios).
